name: IdentiFace
title: Face recognition and analysis, with the age model replaced after testing
summary: A web app on DeepFace that recognises registered people from a webcam or photo, verifies whether two photos show the same person, and estimates age, gender, emotion and ethnicity.

metrics.label: app tabs: Recognise, Verify, Analyse, People, System
minimum face-detection confidence before a face is used
cooldown before the same person is logged again

problem: DeepFace makes face recognition easy to call, but a library isn't a product. You still need a place to register people, a live camera view, a log of who was seen and a way to compare two photos.
The library's default attribute models also have blind spots, and shipping them untested means confidently wrong answers about people.

constraints.label: Thread safety
constraints.text: DeepFace caches models per process and they aren't thread-safe, so every model call runs on one worker thread.

constraints.label: Model swaps
constraints.text: Changing the recognition model makes every stored embedding unusable, because embeddings from different models can't be compared.

constraints.label: Trust
constraints.text: Gender predictions below 75% confidence are flagged as uncertain rather than presented as fact.

architecture.caption: YuNet finds faces and ArcFace embeds them; embeddings are matched by cosine distance against an in-memory index, and FairFace ONNX models estimate age and gender.

sections.heading: Replacing DeepFace's age and gender models
paras: DeepFace's built-in age model was trained mostly on adult celebrities. In my tests it estimated every child as an adult, and its gender model was right 66% of the time (53% for Black faces). I kept DeepFace for detection, recognition, emotion and ethnicity and replaced age and gender with FairFace ViT models in ONNX Runtime.
The new models predict one of 9 age ranges instead of a single number, use the 25% padding they were trained with, and return the full ranked probabilities.

sections.heading: A recognition index that survives model changes
paras: Registered embeddings sit in an L2-normalised matrix in memory, so recognition is one matrix multiplication and a best-distance-per-person check against the model's threshold.

Each embedding records which model produced it. When the configured model changes, every registered photo is re-encoded, so switching from ArcFace to Facenet512 doesn't break the people already registered.

challenges.title: The 'whole image' fallback looked like a face
challenges.text: With enforce_detection off, DeepFace returns the whole image as a face with confidence 0 when it finds none. Faces below 0.5 confidence are now dropped so that fallback is never matched or registered.

challenges.title: Native thread-pool leaks under Flask
challenges.text: Calling models from per-request threads leaked native thread pools. Every model call now goes through a single-worker executor, which also records latency per operation for the System page.

challenges.title: Live recognition flooding the log
challenges.text: A person in front of the webcam is recognised every frame, so a sighting is written at most once a minute per person and source.

outcome: IdentiFace recognises registered people live from the webcam or a photo, marks strangers 'Unknown', logs sightings with snapshots, verifies photo pairs with a similarity score, and analyses age range, gender, emotion and ethnicity.
People can be registered with several photos, renamed or deleted, and a System page shows the loaded models, threshold and latency.
